newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-POLL SHATTERS WOMEN'S 200 FREESTYLE WORLD MARK.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-POLL SHATTERS WOMEN'S 200 FREESTYLE WORLD MARK.

text.p: Olympic champion Claudia Poll shattered her own 200 metres freestyle world short-course record to retain her title with a flourish at the world short-course swimming championships on Friday.
The tall 24-year-old Costa Rican seized the lead from Germany's Antje Buschschulte before the 100-metre mark and spreadeagled the rest of the field as she imperiously forged her way to victory.

She leaped in delight when she saw her winning time on the electronic scoreboard -- one minute 54.17 seconds which carved more than a second from the 1:55.42 world mark she set at the last world short-course championships in Rio de Janeiro in December 1995.

She received her gold medal with a Costa Rican flag draped around her, flanked by China's Nian Yun, who took the silver in 1:56.24, and Slovakia's Martina Moravcova, who repeated her Rio bronze medal performance with third place in 1:56.66.
